comparator.name: Econometrics and Operations Research
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027; current annual guide and adopted regulations, checked 2026-10-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 chart and annual guide establish 60 EC in each year. The first year has ten required 6 EC units, plus noncredit study support and language obligations. The second year has ten 6 EC units including three part-II courses. One part-II replacement needs permission. The selected third year has 30 EC of elective study, Econometrics III, Mathematical Economics III, Financial Econometrics and a 12 EC thesis. The choice uses one broader elective and satisfies both the guide’s one-or-two rule and the chart’s at-most-two rule. The Econometrics III module code resolves the inconsistent title in the chart. The Integrative Practical requires a first-period partial grade of 5.5 or higher from one of the three part-I subjects. The Advanced Practical requires one pass from each of the probability/statistics, programming/numerical methods and part-I subject groups. The Econometrics thesis requires 120 EC including Econometrics II. Financial Econometrics follows Econometrics III. Keep the minor approval, level and non-overlap rules separate from the required credits.
components: Introduction to Econometrics, Operations Research and Mathematical Economics

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Econometrics and Operations Research bachelor, whose current official curriculum lets students choose one of three third-year specialisations: Econometrics, Operations Research or Mathematical Economics. Econometrics and Operations Research are equally central to the programme's identity (both name the degree and both run through a compulsory I-II sequence), and neither is less specialised than the other, so no route is clearly more representative. Econometrics is selected by the neutral tie-break as the first specialisation in the order the official curriculum prints them. The choice was fixed before any UCR course selection and does not depend on UCR fit. The current 2026–2027 thesis entry explicitly refers to the chosen graduation specialisation; the recruitment page names Econometrics first. The three Year-3 electives are instantiated choices under that route, not three simultaneous specialisations.

core: Mathematical analysis, calculus and mathematical reasoning
Probability theory, statistics and statistical inference
Programming, data handling and computational quantitative analysis
Econometrics: regression, estimation, forecasting and multivariate time-series analysis
Operations research: mathematical optimisation, algorithms and decision-making under uncertainty
Mathematical economics: formal models of individual, strategic and market behaviour
Macroeconomics and finance as application foundations
Applying quantitative methods to integrated cases, quantitative research and presenting results to non-specialists
adjacent: Operations Research specialisation and the planning of capacity and service systems
Quantitative analysis of energy systems and sustainable production
questions: How do economic and financial shocks propagate, and what are their short- and long-run effects on inflation, employment and output?
How can scarce hospital capacity such as beds and doctors be planned and used efficiently?
How can production be optimised for lower material and energy use, and how does variability in solar and wind generation affect energy output and electricity prices?

trace: teaches structured and object-oriented programming in Python together with elements of discrete mathematics and computational problem solving, the programming foundation for all later computational work
covers differentiation, integration techniques, complex numbers and differential equations, the calculus foundation that the later modelling courses assume
develops logic, discrete structures and the mathematics of decision-making with applications to algorithm construction, supplying formal reasoning and the discrete foundations of optimisation
treats systems of linear equations, matrices, vector spaces, eigenvalues and Markov chains, the matrix methods used throughout estimation and optimisation
provides a foundation in mathematical statistics: probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation
introduces research design and descriptive and inferential statistics up to analysis of variance, applied in a group research project
develops data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation skills and ends with an independent data-analysis project answering a research question
introduces relational database theory, SQL and query processing, the data-management layer on which large empirical and planning datasets are handled
treats numerical root finding, interpolation, differentiation, integration and differential equations, with explicit attention to algorithmic accuracy and sensitivity to input

Studies linear time-invariant signals, convolution and Fourier/Laplace/Z transforms. It contributes mathematical systems analysis; no state-space, stochastic time-series or financial-shock estimation equivalence is claimed.
teaches the design and experimental performance analysis of algorithms and data structures, on which efficient optimisation procedures depend
studies advanced algorithmic techniques and solution methods for optimisation problems, with emphasis on algorithmic thinking and mathematical modelling
Implements search, constraint satisfaction and linear, discrete and nonlinear optimization in computational problems.
Models decisions under uncertainty through Bayesian networks, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandits.
Fits and diagnoses regression and multivariable models for behavioural data, including categorical outcomes and latent constructs.
introduces regression, classification, resampling and shrinkage methods for prediction, the statistical-learning side of forecasting

teaches OLS, GLS and instrumental-variables estimation, t, F and LM tests and Monte Carlo study of sampling distributions, and requires an empirical paper estimating economic relationships and making predictions
introduces supply and demand, game theory, consumer and firm theory, market structure and the macroeconomics of output, unemployment, inflation and financial markets
analyses national income, growth, inflation, unemployment, business cycles, economic crises and the effects of fiscal and monetary policy
develops advanced microeconomic theory: decision-making under uncertainty, imperfect competition and strategic behaviour, general equilibrium, market efficiency and externalities
Examines biases, heuristics, framing and experiments in economic decision-making; behavioral economic inquiry rather than a formal mathematical-economics sequence.
Studies financial statements, costing and budgeting. Uses discounted cash flow and cost of capital to assess investment projects.
examines fairness and bias, privacy, responsibility and accountability in automated and algorithmic decision systems
Introduces sustainability through planetary boundaries and environmental thresholds; prepares later sustainability study, without establishing technical energy-system design by itself.
extends the sustainability foundation through waves, chemistry and materials science and is the formal gateway to renewable-system design
covers the drivers and impacts of anthropogenic climate change and societal responses including renewable energy systems, the problem that energy-transition analysis addresses
evaluates the environmental impact of products and processes across their whole life cycle and circular-economy strategies, the analytical frame for reducing material and energy use in production
assesses energy-usage patterns and solar, wind and bioenergy options through combined technical and economic analysis, reported to a partner company
Compares renewable technologies, estimates energy yield and studies grids, storage and demand.

analyses market failure, public goods, externalities and taxation with theoretical models and empirical evidence, the welfare framework in which interventions in energy markets and emissions are evaluated
examines the main moral theories and applies them to practical questions including climate change and obligations to future generations

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics and computational optimisation
alternatives.labelReason: The actual courses build mathematical/statistical and programming foundations, applied econometric estimation, AI optimisation and economic analysis. The label avoids promising a dedicated mathematical-economics or finance sequence.
alternatives.concept: Uses mathematics, programming, optimization and econometrics to investigate economic questions. Students build and evaluate quantitative models and examine economic behaviour, inflation and investment. Algorithms and numerical methods support work on computational decisions.
progression: Programming and discrete mathematics start in term one. Year-one mathematical and research foundations precede linear algebra, probability, experimental statistics, algorithms and numerical methods. Optimization and econometrics are in term six.

alternatives.label: Quantitative methods, sustainability and energy
alternatives.labelReason: Climate, materials, renewable technologies and public economics make sustainability and energy the main applications of shared quantitative methods.
alternatives.concept: Uses quantitative methods to study energy and sustainable production. Students compare renewable technologies, assess materials and energy use over a product’s life, and use economics to examine policy. Renewable System Design combines technical and economic analysis in a report for a partner company.
progression: The first-year sustainability and quantitative foundations lead into climate, life-cycle analysis, numerical methods and energy technology. Sustainability Essentials II precedes Renewable System Design. Econometrics and optimization are in term six.
alternatives.distinctness: Eight courses differ in each direction (60 EC). Sustainability foundations, climate, life-cycle analysis, energy technology, renewable-system design, public economics and ethics replace accounting, macroeconomics, behavioural economics and several computing subjects.
traceOverrides: Uses Bayesian networks and Markov decision processes for planning under uncertainty. These methods provide a basis for studying energy decisions.

Provides OLS/GLS/IV estimation, tests and an empirical paper. These general tools can inform economic energy questions; the actual course does not guarantee energy-price time-series or volatility models.

candidates.label: Quantitative analysis of energy systems and sustainable production
Operations Research specialisation: capacity and service planning

selection.assessment: Two directions meet the academic and scheduling requirements. The main option develops computational optimization and applied econometrics. The energy direction adds technology, sustainable production and policy. The available operations and planning methods are already included. The workbook does not support separate specialist sequences in financial shocks, mathematical economics or economic networks.

blocks: Both use differentiation and integration to solve mathematical problems. VU also develops formal analysis.
Both are the dedicated linear-algebra course: systems of equations, matrices, vector spaces and eigenvalues.
Both are the dedicated numerical-methods course: numerical root finding, differentiation, integration and the accuracy of algorithms.
VU continues formal analysis and proof. UCR studies mathematical methods and discrete reasoning in different courses.
Both are the mathematical-probability course: probability theory and discrete and continuous distributions. UCR's course also covers estimation and simulation.
Both cover descriptive and inferential statistics and hypothesis testing. UCR teaches them alongside research design.
Both estimate linear relationships and assess statistical evidence. UCR applies regression, instrumental variables and simulation in an empirical paper.
VU connects probability and inference with academic communication in a dedicated course. UCR develops these skills across several courses.
VU advances to topics including time series and binary outcomes in a second required econometrics course. UCR offers one applied econometrics course.
VU’s elective advances into panel data and multivariate time series. UCR’s signals course studies impulse responses from an engineering perspective.
VU develops models for financial risk and volatility. UCR has no dedicated financial econometrics course.
Both are the introductory programming course in which students learn to write and debug programs for quantitative problem solving.
Both formulate optimization problems and study solution methods. UCR uses search, constraints and linear and discrete optimization in AI.
Both use Markov decision processes to analyse decisions under uncertainty. UCR develops these methods for intelligent agents, while VU also studies multistage stochastic optimization.
VU introduces econometrics, operations research and mathematical economics together. UCR develops related methods across economics, computing and mathematics.
Both are the macroeconomics course: output, inflation, unemployment, business cycles and fiscal and monetary policy.
Both evaluate investments using discounted cash flow and cost of capital. VU also values traded assets and studies portfolios.

Both address choices under uncertainty, strategic behavior and welfare/market efficiency. VU explicitly develops mathematical properties and calculations of decision models, including group choices and game theory. UCR provides related microeconomic theory, with no claim to equal formal breadth.
VU continues its formal economic theory sequence. UCR examines microeconomics, public economics and behaviour in separate courses.
VU’s advanced mathematical economics elective applies formal methods to games and networks. UCR covers selected economic and computational methods across courses.
Both examine ethical issues in quantitative decisions. UCR focuses on bias, privacy and responsibility in AI.
VU integrates its three quantitative disciplines in a dedicated business practical. UCR uses projects within individual courses.
VU continues team case work and technical reporting in a second practical. The UCR energy option includes a partner report on renewable systems.
VU reserves 30 EC for a minor or approved elective study. UCR displays complete course schedules.
VU requires an individual quantitative thesis and poster. UCR’s optional independent research sits outside the displayed schedules.

notes.text: VU develops longer sequences in econometrics, operations research and mathematical economics, with integrated practicals and a 12 EC thesis. UCR covers related methods in economics, mathematics and computing. The energy option adds applied analysis of renewables and sustainable production. Independent research at UCR is optional and sits outside the displayed schedules.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Amsterdam combines econometrics, operations research and mathematical economics. Students use statistics and computing to analyse economic relationships and solve decision problems, then complete an individual quantitative thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: One UCR option connects applied econometrics with economic analysis and computational optimization. The other applies shared quantitative methods to renewable energy, sustainable production and policy.

curriculum.limitation: The final year shown includes 30 EC of elective study, three 6 EC choices and a 12 EC thesis. Entry to the Econometrics thesis requires at least 120 EC, including Econometrics II.
